subject: lavaan and AMOS differences with Wheaton classic data

messages.author: 737df221597ac361
messages.subject: lavaan and AMOS differences with Wheaton classic data
parts:
Hi,
I have compared the results from lavaan and AMOS. I have used the Wheaton classic data covariance matrix. A model with factor loadings of the ﬁrst of the indicators ﬁxed to 1.0, can produce exact results of chi-square and other coefficients, but some minimal differences in variances, when compare lavaan and AMOS results. But a model with the variance of latent variables ﬁxed to 1.0, can produce exact results of coefficients as chi-square, CFI, TLI, and some minimal differences in variances, but some awesome sign differences in some results. To fix to 1.0 variances, I have used the next sintaxis

fit <- sem(wheaton.model, std.lv=TRUE,sample.cov = wheaton.cov,sample.nobs = 932,likelihood = "wishart")



This is the model I have used in lavaan:

wheaton.model <- '


ses     =~ education sei

alien67 =~ anomia67 powerless67

alien71 =~ anomia71 powerless71


alien71 ~ alien67 ses

alien67 ~ ses'



The graphic model in Amos is in the file attached.


lavaan results

Regressions:

  alien71 ~

        ses   -0.233    0.070   -3.316    0.001   -0.151   -0.151

  alien67 ~

    ses       -0.688    0.062  -11.147    0.000   -0.567   -0.567

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: lavaan and AMOS differences with Wheaton classic data
parts:
The direction of the signs is arbitrary. The two models are exactly the same, because:
a * -b is equal to -a * b.

You can set starting values in either Amos or Lavaan that will start the model in a similar place,and give you the same result.

Jeremy
